hostClass: Apple M1 (Virtual, 3 cores), 7 GiB, macOS 15.7.7, Swift 6.1.2 — the GitHub-hosted macos-15-arm64 runner this gate actually runs on
note: The 0.4.0 baseline, re-recorded from the first scheduled CI run (Nightly 30155205374, 2026-07-25) per the plan stated in the previous revision of this file. It was originally recorded on the development machine (Apple M4 4P+6E, 24 GiB, macOS 27, Swift 6.4) at 735980 symbols/s; the hosted runner is a 3-core M1 VM and measured 342668, a 2.15x host-class gap that breached the tolerance on the first run. Thresholds are HOST-CLASS-RELATIVE, so the baseline belongs to the host that runs the gate: this number is the runner's, and a development-machine run will clear it with room to spare (comparison is one-sided, so a FASTER host never fails). Re-record whenever the runner host class changes — the smoke's machine block in the JSON shows it. CAVEAT: this is a single sample from one run on shared, variable hosted hardware; if it flaps, take the low end of several runs rather than widening the tolerance. It gates on ONE metric, stream-throughput, which is stable (about 2 percent intra-run spread in the smoke config; 1.3 percent on the recording run). filter-throughput is deliberately omitted: its smoke-config spread reaches about 17 percent (short runs over a 16 MiB buffer), so gating on it would flap; the smoke still measures and prints it, and the comparator reports any metric absent from this file without gating. Tolerance is wide (35 percent) on purpose: this is a catastrophe canary for a real (roughly 1.5x or worse) engine regression, not a precise perf gate. Precise performance work runs the full swiftfilt-bench battery on a known host (methodology in Benchmarks/README.md). Comparison is one-sided: throughput fails only when median falls below baseline*(1-tolerance). A baseline metric missing from the run fails rather than skips.
